plain_language: A new AI chip launched at the lowest price and fastest speed. Cerebras stock hit a fresh record after a third bank said Buy. A new tool helps measure when AI agents go off track.
findings:
Thursday's evidence cycle resolves into five tightly stacked threads, each of which lands cleanly on one of today's three fresh predictions and densifies the structural-force readings on a small set of prior-week predictions. The cleanest single-session validation is again the Cerebras CBRS tape: a $235.40 close against Wednesday's $224.85 on a fresh post-IPO single-day volume record of 24.1 million shares (the first session crossing the $235 handle), driven by Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore's Thursday pre-market Overweight initiation at a $275 twelve-month target, explicitly framing Wednesday's Goldman Sachs $260 and Citi $245 reads as 'directionally aligned but undershooting the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close revenue ramp.' Moore's DCF model lifts first-half 2027 disclosed-customer revenue to a $1.96B midpoint against the prior Bernstein cohort spread of $1.62B, Goldman Sachs analyst Toshiya Hari's Thursday afternoon refresh raises the prior $260 target to $278 inside the same session, institutional buyside cumulative net position crosses the half-of-float threshold for the first time on CBRS at 52.4 percent, Reuters confirms Russell Investments' index-construction team explicitly flagged Cerebras for prospective Russell 1000 small-to-large-cap migration inclusion in the June 26 reconstitution announcement, and the September 2026 $260 call line crosses 41,200 contracts of open interest as the first six-figure-equivalent build on the $260 strike. Today's fresh Cerebras-Russell-1000-small-to-large-cap-migration-at-June-26-reconstitution prediction lands its three qualifying state-changes inside the trading day itself; the Cerebras-top-tier-sell-side-Buy-initiation-cohort prediction (May 27) compounds with Morgan Stanley making the third bulge-bracket Buy inside a 48-hour window; and the Cerebras-CBRS-above-analyst-band-ceiling-re-rating prediction (May 25) confirms a durable second-session hold above the Jefferies $225 threshold with Street ceiling now in the prediction's named $245-$278 bullish-tier band.

The hardware-plus-routing thread compresses into a single forward-looking inference-stack story. Groq's Thursday formal commercial-availability launch of the LPU-v3 Inference Network ships 1.84 ExaFLOPS BF16 across 18 data-center sites on a 4nm Samsung Foundry process, a 3.2x lift over LPU-v2 with measured throughput of 38,420 tokens-per-second on the Llama-3.1-70B FP8 reference workload at batch size 1024, with Anandtech confirming a 2.4x energy-efficiency improvement (tokens per joule) placing LPU-v3 at the frontier against Nvidia H200, AMD MI325X, and Cerebras CS-3. Groq's Thursday hosted-endpoint price sheet lists Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B at $0.31 per million input tokens (the OpenRouter cohort's lowest floor, an 11-cent undercut from Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's $0.42 Thursday-flip), and Together AI cofounder Vipul Ved Prakash's Thursday-afternoon note records LPU-v3 first-token-latency at 0.082 seconds — the first sub-0.1-second cold-start reading the OpenRouter dashboard has ever recorded against the cohort's blended median of 0.156 seconds. Simultaneously, OpenRouter's scheduled May 28 integration cycle for Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B landed Thursday morning Pacific as a clean catalyst-date hit, with five hosted providers (Together AI, Fireworks AI, DeepInfra, Hyperbolic, Lepton AI) wired in inside the first six trading hours and the model card clearing 4.2 percent of platform daily request volume inside three hours of GA — the fastest cold-start ramp on any Chinese open-weight model since DeepSeek R1 in January 2025 — with Cursor, Cline, Aider, and Continue.dev all marking the SKU as a default-eligible substitute for Claude Opus 4.7 inside the platform's evals-on-the-fly routing primitive. Today's fresh Groq-LPU-v3-majority-of-Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-routed-traffic prediction lands its because and given clauses inside the trading day itself, and the reservoir-routing-default-vLLM-and-SGLang-serving-knob prediction (May 27) gains its so_that-clause composition signal via the Thursday CMU-Meta token-drift paper.

The research-paper cycle delivers the second credible MoE-router primitive inside 48 hours. CMU Catalyst plus Meta FAIR co-published arxiv 2605.11823 'Token-Drift Trajectories: A Causal Probe for Long-Horizon Agentic Coherence Failures' by CMU Catalyst PhD candidate Tianqi Chen, Meta FAIR senior research scientist Naman Goyal, and Catalyst lab director Zhihao Jia, the first publication directly extending Wednesday's Stanford CRFM plus DeepMind reservoir-routing paper (arxiv 2605.10142) by characterizing the failure-mode side rather than the routing-side optimization. The probe instrument the authors call 'token-drift trajectory mapping' traces how the expert-selection sequence diverges from the intended task-policy distribution over multi-turn agentic conversations, demonstrating on the same 145B-parameter MoE backbone that token drift accumulates super-linearly past 12 tool-use turns and that a simple drift-magnitude threshold at the policy-divergence inflection predicts SWE-Bench Verified failure modes with 84.3 percent accuracy. The paper's 'drift-aware checkpoint' primitive composes additively with reservoir routing — lifting the reservoir-routing-augmented backbone from 78.7 to 81.2 on SWE-Bench Verified (a fresh 2.5pp absolute lift on top of Wednesday's uplift) while reducing per-turn router-compute cost by an additional 12.8 percent on the same 8x H100 SXM5 reference node. Simon Willison flagged the paper as the first composition demonstration the agentic-MoE routing-space optimization line has produced; Hacker News surfaced two CoreWeave H100 SXM5 reproductions inside 2.8 percent of the reference sheet inside the same Thursday window. Today's fresh token-drift-trajectory-probes-agentic-coherence-audit-primitive prediction lands its trigger publication directly.

The local-LLM training thread delivers the central structural threshold for the selective-expert-checkpointing default MoE save primitive prediction (May 26). Unsloth shipped v2026.5.28 introducing first-class compatibility with Hugging Face's TRL (Transformer Reinforcement Learning) library v0.16.0 — the first time a competing trainer library has incorporated Unsloth's selective-expert-checkpoint primitive under a permissive Apache 2.0 path. The Daniel Han Chen plus Mike Han Chen author pair posted a Thursday morning Hugging Face Blog joint with TRL maintainer Costa Huang (DRL pioneer formerly at Hugging Face Reinforcement Learning team) confirming the integration, with Daniel Han Chen's Thursday afternoon Twitter thread flagging the TRL compatibility as the most important interoperability landing since Axolotl v0.5 adopted Unsloth's LoRA primitive in October 2024. The release additionally lands a Kimi-K3-Pro 218B MoE port from the Tsinghua University KEG Lab pull request — the cohort's second contribution in a fortnight following the Tuesday MiniMax M2.7 port — lifting the contributed 60B-class recipe count to five, and a router-aware gradient-accumulation bucket scheduler dropping Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B fine-tuning peak combined VRAM by an additional 9.4 percent versus Tuesday's v2026.5.26 baseline. Three independent reproductions on Lambda Labs and Runpod rentals landed inside 2.1 percent of the Daniel Han Chen sheet.

The remaining locked-in older predictions sit correctly silent under ADR-002. The loader-verification reference-set cohort (May 21-25) does not get a fresh state-change today because no agent-loader CVE or framework-default-shipment news landed in the Thursday cycle. The FMRB executive-order signing, OECD GENAI plenary reciprocity perimeter, three-instrument US oversight stack, Mag-7 AI Services revenue-line breakout, AI-accelerator IPO S-1 risk-factor template, and Tenstorrent S-1 / SambaNova confidential-submission predictions all sit silent without fresh secretariat, OSTP, or Corp Fin movement and correctly score outside today's six chosen validation rows.
